text:
nina: Hi team 1st day here. Using company Fedora laptop. WireGuard profile from Okta seems connected but I can't `docker pull registry.redwood.internal:5000/core/base:latest` from my workstation. curl to the registry IP times out, but I can ping 10.240.2.10 (internal IP). Any ideas?
it-support: Welcome! Quick Qs: does `curl -v https://registry.redwood.internal:5000/v2/_catalog` hang or return an error? Also what does `ip route` and `resolvectl status` show?
nina: curl just hangs on TLS handshake. `ip route` shows default via 192.168.1.1 and a route to 10.240.0.0/16 via wg0. `resolvectl status` shows systemd-resolved on 127.0.0.53 and the VPN pushed nameserver 10.240.1.2 but not for the .internal domain.
sam: Sounds like two issues: routing vs DNS. If you can ping the registry internal IP that's routing okay, so TLS handshake hanging likely cert or MTU/proxy issue. What's `sudo iptables -L -n` and are you running docker rootless?
nina: Docker is systemd-managed rootful. iptables shows a policy ACCEPT, no obvious blocks. MTU on wg0 is 1420. Could that cause TLS to stall?
olivia: MTU can cause stalls for TLS if Path MTU or PMTUD ICMP is filtered. Quick test: try `curl --tcp-fastopen --no-buffer -v --connect-timeout 5 https://10.240.2.10:5000/v2/` and `curl --ipv4 --noproxy '*'` to see behavior. Also try lowering wg0 MTU to 1280 temporarily: `sudo ip link set mtu 1280 dev wg0` then retry.
nina: Lowered MTU, same hang. `curl -v https://10.240.2.10:5000/v2/` shows TCP connect OK then TLS handshake stalls on ClientHello.
it-support: If TCP connects but TLS stalls, check if there's an intercepted proxy or middlebox. Also confirm Docker daemon has access to the VPN network namespace; sometimes Docker's bridge network doesn't route to wg0. Can you `docker run --rm -it --network host curlimages/curl https://registry.redwood.internal:5000/v2/`?
nina: Running with --network host ... also hangs.
sam: Ok that narrows it to host-level TLS issue. Another common cause: corporate transparent TLS inspection which expects client cert or SNI. Does the registry use mutual TLS or a private CA?
nina: Registry uses internal CA (company-root.pem). Browser on the host (Firefox) can hit https://registry.redwood.internal:5000 and shows a valid cert. So CA is trusted.
it-support: Two more checks: 1) check /etc/hosts for an override, 2) check systemd-resolved split config for the internal domain. `resolvectl query registry.redwood.internal` and `resolvectl domain` output please.
nina: `resolvectl query registry.redwood.internal` returns correct A and shows server 10.240.1.2. `resolvectl domain` shows no special domain.
olivia: Hmm curious that browser works but curl and docker hang. Could be TLS stack differences (Firefox uses NSS and its own cert store). System curl uses OpenSSL and verifies server cert against system CA. If Docker pulls are failing, ensure the CA is installed at `/etc/docker/certs.d/registry.redwood.internal:5000/ca.crt` and in `/etc/ssl/certs` (update-ca-trust).
nina: I copied company-root.pem to `/etc/docker/certs.d/registry.redwood.internal:5000/ca.crt` and ran `sudo systemctl restart docker`. Still hangs. `openssl s_client -connect 10.240.2.10:5000 -servername registry.redwood.internal -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt` shows handshake timeout after ClientHello.
sam: Since OpenSSL also stalls, not a CA trust problem. Could be SNI required but server not receiving SNI due to DNS -> IP mismatch when kernel sends SYN with different routing table? Another angle: systemd-resolved's stub resolver on 127.0.0.53 can create weird behavior for apps using glibc NSS. Try bypassing resolved: `sudo ln -sf /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf /etc/resolv.conf` (or the opposite depending on distro) and test again.
nina: I had `/etc/resolv.conf` pointing to 127.0.0.53. Switched to the VPN-provided resolv.conf (`/run/NetworkManager/resolv.conf`) and retried. Now openssl connects and returns certificate chain! Docker pull still times out though.
it-support: Good progress. Docker timing out might be because dockerd has a different DNS config. Check `/etc/docker/daemon.json` for dns settings and see `systemctl show --property=Environment docker` for any env. Also check that dockerd picks up the new resolv.conf; you might need to add `--dns 10.240.1.2` in daemon.json and restart dockerd.
nina: daemon.json had nothing. I added `{ "dns": ["10.240.1.2"] }` then `sudo systemctl restart docker`. `docker pull` now progressing!
sam: Nice. To summarize for onboarding notes: 1) systemd-resolved stub can interfere with VPN DNS; for Fedora we prefer pointing /etc/resolv.conf to the NM-managed file. 2) Docker daemon may need explicit DNS configured to reach internal registries. 3) MTU adjustments sometimes help for flaky connections. 4) Temporary workaround: use bastion SOCKS proxy: `ssh -D1080 nina@bastion.redwood` and `docker --config ~/.docker-proxy ...` or `export HTTP_PROXY` for clients.
nina: Will add a short writeup to the new-hires thread. Thanks all!
infra-bot: Docs: https://confluence.redwood/infra/linux-vpn-docker-guide and https://confluence.redwood/infra/registry-cert-setup :white_check_mark:
nina: Follow-up: added notes and pasted the `resolvectl status` snippet (redacted). Everyone helped move quickly 10x!
